principles: Fix the layer where the defect actually originates, not just the first symptom observed
Prefer narrow, targeted catches over broad architectural changes when the blast radius of a wider fix is uncertain
Keep the existing established patterns (duck-typed error matching, real CLI calls over hand-signed evidence) rather than introducing new mechanisms
Every fix must be proven with a RED script before the fix and a GREEN re-run after
drivers: The concurrent-DONE-race loser must never crash with a raw internal error; it must explain itself clearly
The retired lattice-review-channel lane must be structurally rejected everywhere, including in the CLI smoke test that still exercised it as if forceable
Minimize risk to unrelated code paths given both fixes touch shared DONE/REVIEW lifecycle machinery used by every story

options.name: resolve-store-root-broadly
pros: Would fix the class of bug for every future read through ctx.store during a DONE race, not just this one call site
cons: ctx.store is used pervasively across the whole handler layer; changing its root resolution risks unknown ripple effects across every other command
Far larger blast radius than the two confirmed defects in scope

options.name: narrow-catch-and-translate
pros: Matches the existing duck-typed StoryArtifactMissingError catch pattern already used elsewhere in transition-orchestrator.ts
Minimal blast radius: only affects the exact race window this story is fixing
cons: Does not fix a hypothetical similar crash at some other read site if one exists; only this specific one

options.name: leave-channel-lane-forceable-in-tests
cons: Directly contradicts prompt-role-contract-registry.ts's structural retirement of the lane
Smoke test would keep asserting behavior the product code forbids, silently drifting from reality

options.name: reject-channel-lane-and-reroute-through-active-lane
pros: Reuses an existing active lane (test-coverage) instead of inventing a new one
cons: Required fixing a cascade of five dependent issues in the same test file to get back to green

rationale: Both narrow options (narrow-catch-and-translate, reject-channel-lane-and-reroute-through-active-lane) were chosen together: they fix exactly the two confirmed defects with minimal blast radius, reuse existing established patterns, and were already implemented and RED-then-GREEN verified standalone before this story existed, per the user's explicit instruction to prove RED and GREEN for both before bundling into a story.

preMortem.scenario: The clean error-translation catch in transition-orchestrator.ts accidentally swallows a genuinely different StoryArtifactMissingError (e.g. a real typo'd story id), masking it as a false 'concurrent DONE' explanation
preMortem.trigger: A caller passes an invalid or non-existent storyId while the invocation's own ctx.root also happens to not exist for an unrelated reason
preMortem.consequence: A user gets a misleading 'concurrent DONE already completed' message for what is actually a simple invalid-story-id error
preMortem.mitigation: The catch checks BOTH conditions together (StoryArtifactMissingError AND !existsSync(ctx.root)) -- ctx.root not existing on disk is specific to the worktree-deleted-by-DONE scenario; an invalid story id with a normally-existing root would not match and would rethrow the original error unchanged

preMortem.scenario: The stable-root transition lock introduces a new deadlock or starvation pattern not present before
preMortem.trigger: Many concurrent story_advance calls for the same story pile up waiting on the main-repo-rooted lock instead of the worktree-rooted one
preMortem.consequence: Legitimate non-racing callers experience longer waits or timeouts they did not before
preMortem.mitigation: acquireStoryTransitionLock is a bounded-wait mkdir-based lock already used elsewhere in the same ordering (transitionLock before doneMainMergeLock); only the ROOT changed, not the lock semantics, and the worktree-authority-smoke.js test explicitly exercises and passes the concurrent-DONE scenario end-to-end after the change

preMortem.scenario: The channel-lane rejection assertion or the RP-004 lane swap accidentally breaks a different, still-passing part of field-regression-cli-smoke.ts
preMortem.trigger: The cascade of five dependent fixes (readManifest, wording match, dev_memory_finish_decision, reviewRunId binding, 3-lane quorum) interacts badly with an untouched part of the same large test file
preMortem.consequence: The smoke test file regresses somewhere else even though the specific channel-lane assertions now pass
preMortem.mitigation: The full file was re-run end-to-end after all cascade fixes landed and confirmed '✓ field regression CLI smoke passed' with zero errors, not just the specific modified assertions in isolation

preMortem.scenario: The two new RED scripts silently stop proving anything after a future unrelated change, giving false confidence
preMortem.trigger: A later refactor changes the error message wording or the lane-rejection message text that the RED scripts pattern-match against
preMortem.consequence: The RED scripts would report GREEN (defect gone) even if a regression reintroduced the original bug in a differently-worded form
preMortem.mitigation: Both RED scripts are registered in red-b49d4-harness-registration.mjs's REGISTRATION_EXCLUSIONS with an explicit reason, keeping them visible to the meta-guard rather than silently orphaned; they were also manually confirmed to correctly flip from failing (RED, pre-fix) to failing-their-own-assertion (GREEN, post-fix) during this story's own investigation
